01 / THE CHALLENGE

The challenge

Medical education, clinical decision support and hospital documentation presented different needs and adoption barriers. The task was to find where a product could deliver measurable value and fit institutional workflows.

02 / THE APPROACH

The approach

Built Kaya, a virtual AI patient for case-based learning, with adaptive case progression, real-time diagnostic feedback and clinical-performance analytics. Ran a 1-week pilot at Yashwant Ayurvedic Medical College and Hospital, with 370+ medical-student validations. Alongside the pilot, held 100+ conversations with doctors, hospital staff and students.

03 / WHAT CHANGED

What changed

Kaya was Aivana's first product. What I learned from it, and from conversations with doctors and hospital staff, moved the company from student learning toward tools for clinicians. This evidence led to two product pivots: from student learning to clinical decision support, then to clinical documentation.

IN THE DETAILS

Pilot setting

Yashwant Ayurvedic Medical College and Hospital · Kaya, a virtual AI patient for case-based learning · 1 week · 370+ medical-student validations.

IN THE DETAILS

What the conversations revealed

100+ conversations with doctors, hospital staff and students highlighted EHR integration complexity, documentation overhead and uncertainty around reimbursement and data governance. Kano analysis, PESTEL evaluation and financial viability assessments helped compare the opportunities.

IN THE DETAILS

Two decisions to change direction

The Kaya pilot and discovery conversations moved the company from student learning toward tools for clinicians. Conversations with 10 hospital systems then redirected the work toward clinical documentation.

IN THE DETAILS

Research beyond the conversations

Compared 12 clinical AI vendors across positioning, features, pricing and go-to-market strategies. Created five institutional workflow demonstrations and partner-engagement materials informed by research and pilot learnings. Several discussions advanced to pilot proposals; proposals are distinct from commercial deployments.
